messages:
Anna: Quick sync 	6 moving precision decisioning partly into model manifests. Idea: manifest lists precision candidates + tolerance metadata so compiler/runtime have a single authoritative contract. Thoughts?
Ben: Interesting. How does this change runtime behavior today?
Anna: A few wins: deterministic kernel selection at compile-time, explicit fallback chains baked with the model, and offline validation during CI before any rollout.
Claire: Danger: customers expect per-tenant overrides and SLA-based precision controls. If the manifest is canonical, how do we safely offer that flexibility?
Ben: Keep runtime overrides but validate them against manifest bounds. Manifest exposes allowed_bitwidths and max_degradation; overrides must be subsets and cannot increase degradation.
Diego: For Dedicated/Private we need signing and strict versioning on manifests, plus a migration path so existing profiles don't break during rollouts.
Anna: Sketch of proposed manifest fields: precision_candidates, degradation_budget, headwise_flags, confidence_thresholds, fallback_policy_id, validation_artifact_hash, allowed_overrides.
Ben: Example manifest snippet for clarity:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-7b-v3",
  "precision_candidates": ["fp32", "fp8", "int8", "4bit"],
  "degradation_budget": "0.02",
  "confidence_thresholds": {"early_token": 0.6, "final": 0.82},
  "fallback_policy_id": "fallback-v2",
  "validation_artifact_hash": "sha256:abcd1234...",
  "allowed_overrides": ["int8","fp32"]
}
```
Claire: Operationally, FP8 still trips on long-tail prompts. We need token-level degscore telemetry and a fast early-fallback that triggers before user-visible degradation.
Anna: Proposed early-fallback rule: if degscore > X within first N tokens, escalate to higher precision and optionally regenerate last K tokens. That preserves quality but has cost/regeneration complexity.
Diego: Regeneration during streaming breaks many client implementations. Alternative: soft-correct 	6 send a corrective pass (rerank/append) or expose a flag so clients can opt-in for full regeneration.
Ben: We should also include in the manifest latency_delta_estimate and cost_delta_estimate, plus a small quality-anchor vector for quick smoke checks during canaries. Helps ops weigh tradeoffs per endpoint.
Anna: Action items: Ben 	6 draft runtime validation checkpoints (override validation, early-fallback thresholds). Diego 	6 draft signing/versioning + migration playbook for Dedicated/Private. Claire 	6 design customer-override UX and SLA semantics. I'll assemble RFC with manifest schema and rollout plan tomorrow. :thumbsup:
